title: Tooling: preserve exact moment bounds with a 15× faster integer kernel
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

The selected #5413 moment engine spends most of its sampled pricing time reducing intermediate Fractions. This opt-in adapter computes the same forty-term Taylor sum and the same rational remainder with integer recurrences. Every output grid rounding, squaring, logarithm, reciprocal and downstream pricing function is retained. The package includes an algebraic equivalence proof and an authenticated copy of the frozen reference. No predecessor or selected result is edited; no new κ is claimed.

Three alternating fresh-subprocess pairs on Windows / CPython 3.12.2 give median 4.1874 → 0.2770 seconds (15.12×) for 24 actual invoice ranks × 12 distinct exponents, complete signed moments and strict allowances. All six complete mathematical receipts agree exactly. Both earlier and final timing samples are retained. This measures pricing, not complete caller replay speed.

## Task and overlap

`replay-runtime`, scope refined to the user-requested current moment bottleneck. Canonical base refreshed at 32890bc5de034ab8fc93ac88ead7279a6a416d04. Source engine and invoice Git blobs and SHA256 are pinned in SOURCES.json; package-local snapshots make replay Git-free. Related PR672 and PR2552 already use integer exponential kernels. This adapts the classical technique to the current 72-log / 40-exp / 10^65-grid engine and selected invoice; it does not claim a new method.

## Validation

`python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/current-moment-integer-fastpath` passes normal and optimized commands locally. Checks compare complete rational outputs and all 600 exponential invocation/result records, 121 boundary/seeded arguments, exact unrounded Taylor/remainder parts, 35 signed-power cases and the selected lower/ceiling bracket. Actual degree, tail and inward-rounding mutants are detected, as are source/fixture tampering, an omitted paid call and invalid rank. Committed-byte preflight (13 files), official source export and bundle check pass. The snapshot retains one original trailing blank line, so its whitespace warning is inherited.

Rebenchmark with `python3.12 -B research/current-moment-integer-fastpath/benchmark.py --pairs 3 --output /tmp/fresh-benchmark.json`. No timing threshold is used in CI. Hosted Linux/Windows checks are pending. Full source-history preflight is not claimed from this shallow checkout. Full caller replay, whole-repository tests, physical/native/target/precision/compiler/outer admission, Lean and independent human review were not run for this adapter.

## Credit

Chris R / Clear1nsight supplies the reference arithmetic and caller completion. Dillon, Ali Romman, Cao Yifan, Dugongue, Cinna Davis, zxv and the retained lineage supply the construction. PR672 and PR2552 supply related optimization precedents. New material by Joseph Anglada with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

The package README and TASK.json explain the smallest next steps: compare complete caller receipts through a separately reviewed adapter, and use the exact fast path on a changed fully charged physical word. Native validation may dominate full replay; faster arithmetic alone does not improve κ.
